title: Word frequency counter
summary: Count the words in any text and draw a bar chart of the most common ones. You’ll work with strings and chars, a HashMap, sorting with a comparison, and formatted output.

smoke.stdin:
the cat and the hat
the end

milestones.title: Split into words
milestones.build: `words` splits a text into lowercase words. Letters, digits and apostrophes make up a word; anything else separates words. Trim apostrophes off the ends.

milestones.title: Count them
milestones.build: `count` builds a `HashMap` from each word to how often it appears. The `entry(…).or_insert(0)` pattern from the Book does exactly this.

milestones.title: The most frequent
milestones.build: `top` collects the map into a `Vec`, sorts it by count (largest first) and then by word, and keeps the first `n`. `sort_by` with `cmp(…).then_with(…)` does both orders at once.

milestones.title: Stop words
milestones.build: `remove_stop_words` takes common words like `the` and `and` out of the counts. It borrows the map mutably, so the caller’s map changes.

milestones.title: Stats
milestones.build: `stats` fills in a `Stats` struct: total words, different words and the longest word. Count characters with `chars().count()`, not `len()`, which counts bytes.

milestones.title: A bar chart
milestones.build: `histogram` draws one line per word. `format!("{w:<pad$}")` pads to a width you choose at run time, and `"#".repeat(n)` draws the bar. Then run it: `cargo run -- Cargo.toml`.
